name: Pure Autonomic Failure

criteria.description: Chronic orthostatic hypotension (>=20/10 mmHg drop within 3 min standing) with associated symptoms
Absence of central neurological features (no parkinsonism, no cerebellar ataxia, no cognitive decline suggestive of DLB)
Evidence of peripheral autonomic denervation (low supine norepinephrine levels)
No identifiable secondary cause of autonomic failure

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Chronic orthostatic hypotension with generalized autonomic failure in the absence of central neurological features or secondary causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: PAF is an alpha-synucleinopathy; ~15-30% may phenoconvert to MSA, PD, or DLB over years. Requires longitudinal follow-up.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Severe orthostatic hypotension with isolated autonomic failure and no motor or cerebellar signs
pathognomonic.notes: Defining characteristic is autonomic failure without CNS involvement

rare.notes: May herald phenoconversion to MSA or DLB
Ischemic pain in neck/shoulders from hypoperfusion on standing

laboratory: Absent or blunted norepinephrine rise on standing
imaging: Reduced cardiac MIBG uptake (postganglionic sympathetic denervation)
Normal brain MRI (no pontine, cerebellar, or putaminal atrophy)
other: Autonomic function testing: severe adrenergic, sudomotor, and cardiovagal failure
QSART: absent or reduced sweat output
Valsalva maneuver: absent phase IV overshoot

distinguishingFeatures: MSA has cerebellar or parkinsonian motor features
MSA has central (preganglionic) pattern with normal cardiac MIBG
PAF has peripheral (postganglionic) pattern with reduced MIBG
AAG often has subacute onset and may have ganglionic AChR antibodies
Diabetic neuropathy has concurrent diabetes mellitus
Diabetic neuropathy usually has coexisting peripheral neuropathy

redFlags: Development of parkinsonian features (may indicate phenoconversion to MSA or PD)
Cognitive decline (suggests Lewy body dementia phenoconversion)
REM sleep behavior disorder (risk factor for phenoconversion)
references: Kaufmann H, et al. Natural history of pure autonomic failure: A United States prospective cohort. Ann Neurol. 2017;81(2):287-297.
Goldstein DS, et al. Pure autonomic failure: Insights from clinical research. Clin Auton Res. 2020;30(3):187-193.
Singer W, et al. Pure autonomic failure: Predictors of conversion to clinical CNS involvement. Neurology. 2017;88(12):1129-1136.
